title: Graph Algorithms for Network Analysis
subtitle: A Textbook of Methods: From Traversal to Community Detection
author: Jane Example
affiliation: Department of Computer Science, Example University
subject: Algorithms for analyzing large graphs and networks
keywords: graphs, shortest paths, centrality, community detection, spectral methods
application_context: the analysis of real networks (social, transport, biological)
purpose: Teach, from first principles, every method of the course plan (docs/requirements.md): traversal, shortest paths, centrality, clustering and community detection, spectral methods, and how they combine into one analysis pipeline.
reader: A graduate student or engineer starting research on network analysis. Comfortable with Python, basic linear algebra and probability. Reads the book alone, without a lecturer.
code_policy: Python 3.10+, NumPy and SciPy only (no NetworkX in reference implementations, so that every algorithm is visible). PEP 8, short docstrings, no unicode in source.
length_rule: 16-22 pages for the Essential chapters (up to 24 when the material needs it), 12-20 pages for the others.

chapters.title: Networks and the Questions We Ask
chapters.scope: What a network is, the questions of the book, the analysis pipeline previewed, map of all methods with their priority, how to read the book.

chapters.title: The Toolbox: Graphs, Matrices and Probability
chapters.scope: Graph representations, adjacency and Laplacian matrices, degree distributions, basic probability, big-O, the Python stack.

chapters.title: Breadth-First and Depth-First Search
chapters.scope: BFS/DFS, connected components, bipartiteness, topological order, proofs and complexity.

chapters.title: Shortest Paths
chapters.scope: Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, negative cycles, all-pairs methods, correctness proofs.

chapters.title: Centrality and PageRank
chapters.scope: Degree, closeness, betweenness (Brandes), eigenvector centrality, PageRank as a Markov chain, power iteration convergence.

chapters.title: Community Detection
chapters.scope: Modularity, Louvain, spectral clustering, evaluation of partitions, resolution limit.

chapters.title: An Analysis Pipeline
chapters.scope: How the methods combine on a real dataset, interfaces, what guarantees survive, research directions.

chapters.title: Evaluating Network Methods
chapters.scope: Benchmarks, synthetic generators, metrics with formulas, statistics and reporting, reproducibility.

appendices.title: The Course Plan
appendices.scope: The schedule mapped to chapters, exercises and milestones, with a traceability table.

appendices.title: Mathematical Refresher
appendices.scope: Linear algebra, probability and optimization facts the chapters rely on, each naming the chapters that depend on it.

appendices.title: Hints and Solutions to Selected Exercises
appendices.scope: Assembled from the per-chapter solution files.
